items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's first choice is d4.
At depth 16 the engine rates Re4 lower than d4.
At depth 16 the engine rates d3 lower than d4.
At depth 16 the engine rates Re2 lower than d4.
Black attacks the f2 pawn twice (knight and queen).
White defends the f2 pawn 2 times.

hints: Black has a knight and a queen aimed at the same pawn. How many White pieces guard it?
White has not yet used a pawn in the centre. Which one can move?
The d-pawn can advance two squares.
items.explain: d4 was Capablanca's move in the game. At depth 16 the engine rates it first; Re4, d3 and Re2 are rated at least six tenths of a pawn lower. The engine does not say why; it says this centre move keeps the advantage.

feedback_by_move.e1e4: Re4 is rated at least 0.6 pawn lower than d4 by the engine at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.d2d3: d3 is rated at least 0.6 pawn lower than d4 by the engine at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.e1e2: Re2 is rated at least 0.6 pawn lower than d4 by the engine at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's first choice is hxg4.
At depth 16 the engine rates Qxf2 at least 2.5 pawns lower than hxg4.
At depth 16 the engine rates Bg5 at least 2.5 pawns lower than hxg4.
The bishop on g4 attacks the queen on f3.
hxg4 is a legal capture.

hints: Which White piece is under attack, and by what?
White can remove the attacker instead of moving the queen.
items.explain: hxg4 was the game move. It removes the bishop that attacks the queen. At depth 16 the engine rates hxg4 first and Qxf2 or Bg5 at least 2.5 pawns lower. Black then has the check Bh2+, which the next steps show.

feedback_by_move.f3f2: Qxf2 takes a knight but is rated at least 2.5 pawns lower than hxg4 by the engine at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.c1g5: Bg5 is rated at least 2.5 pawns lower than hxg4 by the engine at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: White is in check.
The king's legal squares are d3, f3.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Kd3.
At depth 16 the engine rates Kf3 at least five pawns lower than Kd3.
At depth 16 the engine rates Be6 at least five pawns lower than Kd3.
At depth 16 the engine rates Be3 at least five pawns lower than Kd3.
At depth 16 the engine rates Qe3 at least five pawns lower than Kd3.

hints: The king is in check. Ways to meet a check: move away, block, capture. Which are available?
Blocking on the e-file costs a piece each time. Where can the king itself go?
The king can step to a square on the d-file.
items.explain: Kd3 was the game move. At depth 16 the engine rates Kd3 first. The king has only two legal squares, d3 and f3; Kf3 and each of the blocks Be6, Be3 and Qe3 are rated at least five pawns lower. In the game the king walked out of the check; it did not block.

feedback_by_move.e2f3: Kf3 is rated at least five pawns lower than Kd3 by the engine at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.b3e6: Be6 blocks, but the engine at depth 16 rates it at least five pawns lower than Kd3.
feedback_by_move.d2e3: Be3 blocks, but the engine at depth 16 rates it at least five pawns lower than Kd3.
feedback_by_move.h3e3: Qe3 blocks, but the engine at depth 16 rates it at least five pawns lower than Kd3.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bd5.
At depth 16 the engine rates a4 lower than Bd5.
At depth 16 the engine rates g5 lower than Bd5.
After Bd5 two White pieces attack f7 (bishop and queen).
Black defends f7 twice (king and rook).

hints: Black's king has few defenders. Which pawn in front of it can White attack?
White's queen already looks along the f-file. Which piece can add a second attacker to the same square?
The bishop on b3 can go to the long diagonal.
items.explain: Bd5 was the game move. It adds a second attacker to f7, which Black defends twice. At depth 16 the engine rates Bd5 first; a4 is at least 0.5 pawn and g5 at least one pawn lower. The engine does not call it forced; the finish ten moves later shows what the extra attacker did.

feedback_by_move.a2a4: a4 is rated at least 0.5 pawn lower than Bd5 by the engine at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.g4g5: g5 is rated at least one pawn lower than Bd5 by the engine at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bxf7+.
The engine finds a forced mate in six after Bxf7+.
At depth 16 the engine rates Ra8 at least three pawns lower than Bxf7+.
Black's rook on e3 attacks the queen on f3.
White attacks f7 with the bishop and the queen.

hints: Black's rook attacks White's queen. Must White move it, or can a check come first?
Two White pieces aim at f7. Count its attackers and defenders.
Take on f7 with the bishop, giving check.
items.explain: Bxf7+ was the last move of the game score. The engine at depth 16 finds a forced mate in six after it and rates Ra8 at least three pawns lower. The queen is attacked, but a check comes first.

feedback_by_move.a6a8: Ra8 is rated at least three pawns lower than Bxf7+ by the engine at depth 16.
